rules.title: Comment or doc line that credits an AI tool
rules.instead: Delete the line. Who wrote the code is recorded in git, not in the file.

rules.title: Chat-style phrase left in a comment or doc
rules.instead: Delete it, or say what the code does: "Retries twice on timeout" rather than "Here is the updated code as requested".

rules.title: AI tool file tracked or about to be committed
rules.instead: Add it to .gitignore and untrack it with `git rm --cached`; the local file keeps working.

rules.title: AI co-author trailer in a commit message
rules.instead: Leave the trailer out of new commits. Changing pushed commits needs a history rewrite, so only do it when asked.

rules.title: "Generated with" line in a commit message
rules.instead: Describe the change instead: "Add CSV export for orders".

rules.title: Comment that repeats the next line
rules.instead: Delete it. Keep comments for why, not what: "Cents avoid float rounding" rather than "Set the total".

rules.title: Section banner in a short file
rules.instead: Delete the banner; a short file reads fine without dividers.

rules.title: Doc comment longer than the code it describes
rules.instead: One line is enough for a small function: "Formats cents as dollars."

rules.title: "This function ..." comment on a small function
rules.instead: Delete it if the name says the same thing, or start with the verb: "Returns the active users."

rules.title: Catch block that only rethrows the same error
rules.instead: Remove the try/catch; the error propagates the same way without it.

rules.title: Catch block that only logs and carries on
rules.instead: Handle the error, or let it propagate. Logging and continuing hides failures.

rules.title: Empty catch block
rules.instead: Handle the error or let it propagate. If ignoring it is intended, say why in a comment.

rules.title: Handler that catches everything
rules.instead: Catch the errors you expect: `except OSError:` rather than `except:`.

rules.title: Null check on a value that cannot be null
rules.instead: Remove the check; a new object or literal is never null.

rules.title: Interface with a single implementation
rules.instead: Use the class directly until a second implementation (or a test double) needs the interface.

rules.title: Factory that always builds the same thing
rules.instead: Call the constructor where the object is needed.

rules.title: Function that only forwards its arguments to another function
rules.instead: Call the inner function directly, or export it under the name you need.

rules.title: Config object used in one place
rules.instead: Inline the value where it is used.

rules.title: Variable name that says nothing about its content
rules.instead: Name what it holds: `activeUsers` rather than `data`, `invoiceTotal` rather than `result`.

rules.title: Function name with no domain meaning
rules.instead: Name what it does: `indexInStockItemsBySku` rather than `processData`.

rules.title: utils or helpers file collecting unrelated functions
rules.instead: Move each function next to the code that uses it, or into a module named for what it does.

rules.title: Name that does not follow the project's naming style
rules.instead: Use the style the rest of the project uses for this kind of name.

rules.title: File name that does not follow the project's file naming
rules.instead: Rename the file to the project's style and update its imports.

rules.title: File indented differently from the rest of the project
rules.instead: Re-indent the file with the project's indentation, or run the project's formatter.

rules.title: Source file nothing refers to
rules.instead: Delete it if it is unused. If something loads it by name, mention it where it is run (package.json, CI, README).

rules.title: Scratch, debug or backup file left in the project
rules.instead: Delete it, or move it into the project's tests or scripts and refer to it from there.

rules.title: Commented-out code
rules.instead: Delete it; git keeps the old version.

rules.title: Debug logging or breakpoint left in the code
rules.instead: Remove it, or use the project's logger at the right level.

rules.title: Placeholder TODO or elided-code marker
rules.instead: Do the work, or write a specific TODO with an owner or ticket: "TODO(ABC-12): retry on 429".

rules.title: Function stub that does nothing or throws "not implemented"
rules.instead: Implement it or remove it and its callers.

rules.title: Marketing or filler wording
rules.instead: Say what it does in plain words: "Retries failed uploads" rather than "A robust, seamless upload experience".

rules.title: Emoji in docs, comments, logs or commit subjects
rules.instead: Drop the emoji; the words carry the meaning.

rules.title: Very large commit touching many areas
rules.instead: Split future work into focused commits, one change each.

rules.title: Commit message laid out like a generated report
rules.instead: A subject line and, if needed, a short paragraph on why: "Add CSV export\n\nFinance needs monthly exports."

rules.title: Commit subject in a different format from the rest of the history
rules.instead: Use the format the history already uses.
